items.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: Well they treated us a little better on Woody Herman’s band than the other bands like Glenn Miller, Tommy Dorsey, which were known as ghost bands because the leader had died.

ctx.x: I assume when you were with Woody Herman maybe the road travel had improved some? Or was it still —

Well they treated us a little better on Woody Herman’s band than the other bands like Glenn Miller, Tommy Dorsey, which were known as ghost bands because the leader had died. But they had to sleep on the bus a lot, where Woody’s band never, we never had to sleep on the bus. There would always be a hotel. You wouldn’t make a lot of money at all. I hardly saved any money in those two years. So you know going in that you’re not going to make a lot of money, you’d better do it for the love of it and opportunities…
